chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan) from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the fasting person use siwak (tooth-stick) with water and a moist stick, tasting it? He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible
key_terms.يَسْتَاكُ: To use siwak / to clean teeth with a stick

ai.seo_question: Does using siwak with water break the fast according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the incidental taste of water or moisture from the siwak does not constitute eating or drinking, thereby preserving the validity of the fast. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between mere sensory perception and the actual consumption of substances, reflecting the practical ease granted to believers in maintaining hygiene during Ramadan.
